9.9.2. qnav.quantum.realistic

9.9.2.1. realistic.py

summary:

Provides quantum sensors with realistic implementations. Extends from the base quantum sensor and includes realistic physics for capturing measurements.

author:

Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk

version:

1.0.0 - First full implementation of class.

class qnav.quantum.realistic.ColdAtomInterferometer(num_of_atoms: int = 1000000.0, atom_mass: float = 2.20693925e-25, sensor_length: float = 0.5, beam_width: float = 0.01, eta: float = 0.3, time_pulse: float = 0.16, recoil_velocity: float = 0.007)[source]

Parameters used for defining a Cold Atom Interferometer. These properties describe the qualities of an ultra-cold atom interferometer, which is used for capturing quantum accelerations and angle rates.

class qnav.quantum.realistic.QuantumIMU(full_frequency: float, imu_frequency: float, accelerometer_errors: ~qnav.measurement.error_properties.ErrorProperties, gyroscope_errors: ~qnav.measurement.error_properties.ErrorProperties, interferometer: ~qnav.quantum.realistic.ColdAtomInterferometer, sensor_axis: ~qnav.measurement.platform.SensorAxis = <qnav.measurement.platform.SensorAxis object>, duty_cycle: float = 0.5, start_time: float = 0.0, rand_seed: int = None)[source]

Quantum IMU that uses an ultra-cold atom interferometer for measurements. This extends from the base concept quantum IMU by replacing the acquiring of measurement methods with realistic implementations. These feature

take_measurement(est_time: float, ground_truth: GroundTruth)[source]

Samples from the ground truth to collect data to produce measurements. Using the ground truth, captures the current acceleration and angles rates at the time. A series of these are required to produce a measurement before fusion.

Parameters:

  • est_time (float) – The estimated time the measurement of the sensor is expected to be captured at (in seconds).

  • ground_truth (GroundTruth) – The corresponding ground truth data.

reset()[source]

Resets the sensor, clearing all previous measurements. Normally used directly after fusion.

qnav.quantum.realistic.ang_diff(a: float, b: float) → float[source]

Calculate the difference between two angles (in radians).

Parameters:

  • a (float) – The first angle value.

  • b (float) – The second angle value.

Returns:

The difference between the given angles.

Return type:

float
